findings.quote: Insider alignment rests on equity compensation rather than large personal stakes
findings.issue: Pay/ownership claim with no proxy support. The captured proxy excerpt (CD&A executive summary and the ownership table) never describes how executives are paid in equity or how equity pay aligns them. The brief requires every pay claim to rest on the proxy excerpt; this one is inferred.
findings.fix: Cut the equity-compensation clause. Read the ownership figure for the holder instead: 307,933 shares (under 1%) as of August 29, 2025 gives insiders no blocking or control position, so outside holders carry governance. Do not characterize pay structure unless it is on the surface.

findings.quote: The current ratio fell to 1.68 from 4.37 in FY25 because the remaining convertible debt now sits in current liabilities.
findings.issue: Unsupported causal claim. The press-release balance sheet shows the current portion of long-term debt rose to $1,596.9 million from $10.6 million, but nothing on the surface says that current debt is convertible notes. The same inference recurs in sections.risks.idiosyncratic[3] ("the current portion of debt keeps the issue live") and in sections.management.capitalAllocation ("The remaining convertible notes"). Accounts payable ($567.4M vs $225.2M) and accrued payroll also rose, so the current-portion line is not the only driver.
findings.fix: Say what the balance sheet shows: the current portion of long-term debt rose to $1,596.9 million from $10.6 million, which lowered the current ratio. Do not call that debt convertible unless a Context excerpt says so. In risks.idiosyncratic[3], tie dilution to the risk factor ("dilution related to our convertible notes") without asserting which debt line holds the notes.

findings.quote: Industrial lasers, 3D sensing and LiDAR remain smaller, longer-dated options that management expects to add to the market opportunity over time.
findings.issue: Two unsupported elements. (1) "smaller": no industrial-laser, 3D-sensing or LiDAR revenue appears anywhere on the surface; the only split is Components and Systems. (2) Over-attribution: the MD&A says LiDAR and in-cabin 3D sensing "will over time significantly add to our long-term market opportunity". It does not say this about industrial lasers.
findings.fix: Drop "smaller". Attach the market-opportunity statement only to LiDAR and in-cabin 3D sensing, quoting the MD&A wording. Describe industrial lasers only as the MD&A does (precision material processing) or omit them.

findings.quote: Total debt was $3.2B and net debt $1.2B.
findings.issue: Silent source disagreement, and it contradicts another section. The vendor Facts give total debt of $3.2B (up from $2.6B in FY25). The press-release balance sheet in Context gives current portion $1,596.9M plus long-term debt $40.5M, about $1.64B, down from about $2.57B. sections.management.capitalAllocation says equitization "cut debt", which matches the release and contradicts the $3.2B figure used here. A reader also cannot reconcile $3.2B debt less $2.7B cash with $1.2B net debt.
findings.fix: Say once, in balanceCommentary, that the vendor total-debt figure ($3.2B) and the release balance sheet (current portion $1,596.9 million and long-term debt $40.5 million) disagree, and state which one the report uses. Then make capitalAllocation consistent with that choice.

findings.quote: Its real cost is dilution: diluted shares used in the Q4 calculation were 84.6 million against 72.0 million a year earlier.
findings.issue: Quantity mismatch. Q4 FY26 is a loss period, so the 84.6M diluted figure equals basic and excludes dilutive securities. Q4 FY25's 72.0M is a true diluted count. Comparing them understates the current diluted base and does not isolate the effect of equitization. The surface has a like-for-like measure: common shares issued and outstanding were 88.6M at June 27, 2026 against 69.8M at June 28, 2025, plus 2.9M preferred shares now outstanding.
findings.fix: Use the balance-sheet share counts (88.6 million common shares against 69.8 million, plus 2.9 million preferred shares outstanding at June 27, 2026). Alternatively, note that the Q4 FY26 diluted count equals basic because of the loss.
findings.note: Addressed: the analystCommentary no longer compares the share counts, and risks.idiosyncratic[3] uses the balance-sheet counts (88.6M vs 69.8M common, plus 2.9M preferred).

findings.quote: Institutional holders of 5% or more included The Vanguard Group at 10.2%, FMR LLC at 9.8% and BlackRock Inc. at 8.8%.
findings.issue: Stale fact presented as current. The percentages are computed on 70,843,924 shares outstanding as of August 29, 2025. Since then common shares have risen to 88.6M after equitization, so each stake is now a smaller percentage. Vanguard's 10.2% also rests on a Schedule 13G/A dated February 13, 2024, more than two years before the filing. The sentence carries none of this.
findings.fix: Date the stakes to August 29, 2025 (and Vanguard's to its February 13, 2024 13G/A). Say they were computed on 70,843,924 shares, before equitization lifted common shares to 88.6 million, so current percentages are lower. Then say what the holder base means, for example that no single holder controls a vote.

findings.quote: Wajid Ali is executive vice president and chief financial officer per the same proxy.
findings.issue: Stale fact as current. The proxy lists Mr. Ali as CFO among the "Executive officers at the end of fiscal year 2025", a date more than a year before this 10-K. Present tense presents it as current. The same paragraph also asserts "FY26 results show that repositioning taking hold", which credits the CEO for the results without anything on the surface that links the two.
findings.fix: Write "was executive vice president and chief financial officer at the end of fiscal year 2025, per the October 2025 proxy". Recast the FY26 sentence as the analyst's view, and add the counter-reading the proxy itself supplies: Mr. Lowe had hired the entire management team and held the most critical customer relationships, which is a transition risk.

findings.quote: Per the proxy statement dated October 2025, the board chair and CEO roles are separate, and the chair, Penelope A. Herscher, is an outside, independent director.
findings.issue: Restatement, not judgment (rubric item 4). The paragraph lists board facts: separate roles, eight independent directors, three committees, 15 meetings and no related-person transactions. It never says what they mean for a holder, and it gives no counter-case. The dating caveat at the end is good.
findings.fix: Keep the facts dated, then reach a view. For example, an independent chair and no related-person transactions above $120,000 leave little governance discount to apply. Name the counter-reading on the surface: the risk factors list Delaware-law and bylaw provisions that "may make a merger, tender offer or proxy contest difficult".

findings.quote: FY27E revenue of $6.3B and EPS of $21.78 are broadly delivered, but supply limits and a maturing cycle compress the multiple as earnings grow. The shares track earnings rather than re-rate.
findings.issue: Base case is not anchored (rubric item 6). The $1,100 implied price is tied to no multiple, guided figure or worked argument, so the reader cannot tell how $21.78 of EPS becomes $1,100. "Compress the multiple" is also hard to square with a Base price above today's $1,045.78 while the stock already trades at 30.1x FY28E EPS. Read against FY28E, $1,100 implies a multiple at or above today's.
findings.fix: Anchor Base in words to a multiple already on the page, for example that it holds roughly today's 30.1x on FY28E EPS of $34.73 rather than compressing it. Or state which multiple and which earnings year produce $1,100. Remove "compress the multiple" unless the arithmetic shows compression.
findings.note: Addressed: Base is now anchored in words to about today's 30.1x on FY28E EPS of $34.73, with modest upside as estimates firm.

findings.quote: We put half the weight on Base at $1,100, a quarter on Bull at $1,400 and a quarter on Bear at $620. The probability-weighted value lands close to the current price, so the expected upside is small.
findings.issue: Probabilities and implied prices are restated from the scenario table rather than argued, and the weighted-value claim appears in three places: executiveSummary.thesis ("Our probability-weighted value lands close to the current price"), here, and finalRecommendation.body[1] ("our probability-weighted value sits close to the current price"). None of them quotes the rendered weighted fair value or expected upside, so the claim never resolves to a number. "Bull adds about a third to the price; Bear removes about two-fifths" also derives new figures. The bear-case downside is renderable; the Bull upside is not.
findings.fix: In scenarioCommentary, argue why Base carries 50% and the tails 25% each instead of restating the weights. Quote the weighted fair value, expected upside and bear-case downside once, here. Have the thesis and the final recommendation point to that view in words. Replace "about a third" with a statement the page renders.
findings.note: Addressed: the weighted fair value ($1,055), expected upside (+0.9%) and bear-case downside (-40.7%) are quoted once, in scenarioCommentary, and the thesis points to Valuation.

findings.quote: the company's own history shows customers building and then cutting inventory, which drove FY24 revenue down 23.1% and gross margin to 18.5%
findings.issue: Cross-section repetition of the FY24 downturn. The same story with the same figures appears in analystCommentary ("like FY24, when revenue fell 23.1%"), executiveSummary.risks[0] ("the pattern that cut FY24 revenue", an acceptable pointer), valuation.scenarios[2].driver ("as in FY24 when revenue fell 23.1% and gross margin dropped to 18.5%"), valuation.scenarioCommentary ("this company's revenue fell 23.1% in FY24 when customers cut inventory"), businessMoat.durability ("gross margin falling to 18.5% in FY24 when demand turned") and here. That is five argued retellings.
findings.fix: Tell the FY24 story with its figures once, in risks.idiosyncratic[0] or the Bear driver. Elsewhere refer back in words (for example "the FY24 inventory cycle") without repeating 23.1% and 18.5%. Keep the exec-summary pointer.

findings.quote: GAAP net loss of $6.9 billion, or $92.96 per diluted share, comes from the one-time, non-cash $7.8 billion loss on debt extinguishment tied to equitizing convertible notes.
findings.issue: Cross-section repetition of the equitization/dilution story. The $7.8 billion non-cash loss and the GAAP-loss explanation appear in analystCommentary ("The headline GAAP loss of $6.9 billion is a one-time, non-cash $7.8 billion loss"), here, and management.capitalAllocation ("produced the $7.8 billion non-cash loss"). The dilution consequence is argued in analystCommentary, executiveSummary.risks[3], management.capitalAllocation, risks.idiosyncratic[3] and management.insiderOwnership ("the share count has risen since the convertible notes were equitized"). The unusable GAAP P/E is also stated twice: incomeCommentary ("The GAAP P/E of -11.2x is therefore not a usable valuation anchor") and valuation.multiplesCommentary ("the GAAP P/E of -11.2x is distorted by the extinguishment loss").
findings.fix: Explain the loss once, in incomeCommentary. Argue dilution once, in risks.idiosyncratic[3] or capitalAllocation, and have the rest refer back in words. State the P/E distortion only in multiplesCommentary.

findings.quote: We would revisit on a pullback, or if results show FY28E revenue of $9.7B is conservative.
findings.issue: Paraphrased sentence in two sections. valuation.scenarioCommentary already says "We would turn more constructive on a pullback that improves the reward/risk, or on evidence that FY28E is conservative." Most of the rest of the final recommendation also restates earlier figures: 83.2%, 17.4%, $300.1M and 30.1x FY28E EPS, each already argued in analystCommentary, financials or valuation. "near the 52-week high" repeats the thesis and analystCommentary.
findings.fix: Keep the what-would-change-our-mind trigger in one place, preferably the final recommendation, with a concrete level. Cut it from scenarioCommentary. Let the final recommendation summarize in words and point back instead of re-quoting the headline figures.

findings.quote: Management guides the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 to $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion of revenue and $4.05 to $4.35 of non-GAAP diluted EPS
findings.issue: Cross-section repetition of the guide and product drivers. The $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion guide appears in analystCommentary, executiveSummary.catalysts[0] and here. OCS and 1.6T appear in catalysts[1], growth.points[2] and the Bull driver. In-rack CPO/ELS/NPO appear in catalysts[2] and growth.points[3]. Customer concentration is argued in executiveSummary.risks[1], businessMoat.moatFactors[2] and risks.idiosyncratic[1]. Tariffs with China and Thailand appear in executiveSummary.risks[2] and risks.systemic. 31.1x trailing sales appears in analystCommentary, multiplesCommentary and risks.systemic. The consensus +10.9% appears in thesis and multiplesCommentary. The FY26 Components +79.7% and Systems +90.7% appear in incomeCommentary and businessMoat.segments[0].body.
findings.fix: Give each figure one home. Guide figures go in growth (catalysts point to them in words). Product-type growth goes in businessMoat.segments. 31.1x sales and the +10.9% consensus upside go in multiplesCommentary. Customer concentration goes in risks.idiosyncratic. Elsewhere, refer back without the numbers.

findings.quote: Demand is outpacing supply and the company is allocating output, which signals capability that is hard to replicate quickly.
findings.issue: Inference the source does not make, and it points the wrong way. The MD&A says demand outpacing supply "has required us to make decisions on supply allocation". That shows a capacity shortfall, not a hard-to-replicate capability, and it is equally consistent with customers buying from whoever has supply. The counter-reading (customers may qualify second sources while Lumentum is short) is not named.
findings.fix: Argue the manufacturing moat from what the MD&A does say ("our volume manufacturing capability") and present allocation as evidence of tight supply. Name the counter-case that shortage invites customers to qualify alternatives.

findings.quote: No share repurchases are recorded for FY26, and the company does not pay a dividend.
findings.issue: Data gap read as a fact. The Facts cash-flow table shows "—" for FY26 share repurchases, which means the figure was not captured, not that it was zero. The sentence reads as if no buybacks occurred.
findings.fix: Say the FY26 repurchase figure is not available in the pack, or drop the buyback clause. Keep the dividend statement, which the risk factors support.

findings.quote: The pack carries no peer multiples, so we do not benchmark against named competitors.
findings.issue: Voice. "The pack" is internal process language that the reader does not know about. Avoiding ungrounded peers is right, but the sentence describes the desk's workflow instead of the valuation.
findings.fix: Drop the sentence, or write "We value LITE on its own estimates rather than against peers" without referring to the pack.

findings.quote: in the CEO's words, the first signs optics are penetrating in-rack connectivity
findings.issue: Attributed as the CEO's words but paraphrased. The release says "the first signs that optics are starting to penetrate in-rack connectivity". "starting to" is the hedge, so the exact wording is the point.
findings.fix: Quote verbatim: "the first signs that optics are starting to penetrate in-rack connectivity".

findings.quote: Base carries half the weight because the near-term guide and supply allocation make the next few quarters unusually visible; a miss on FY27E would need a demand break, not just execution slippage.
findings.issue: Introduced by the rewrite. The new probability argument rests on two unsupported claims (rubric items 2 and 6). (1) The guide covers one quarter, the first quarter of fiscal 2027, so it does not make "the next few quarters" visible. (2) "a miss on FY27E would need a demand break, not just execution slippage" contradicts the report's own risks.idiosyncratic[2]: "meeting guidance depends on the company and its contract manufacturers adding output on time while supply is being allocated". The forward-looking statements in the press release also list capacity and contract-manufacturer delivery among the factors that could cause a miss. The 50% Base weight therefore rests on an argument the page itself undercuts.
findings.fix: Argue the Base weight from what the surface supports: one quarter of guidance, plus consensus FY27E and FY28E paths that assume delivery. Then name execution on capacity as a way Base could miss, consistent with risks.idiosyncratic[2]. Drop "next few quarters" and the demand-break-only claim.

findings.quote: Those percentages were computed on 70,843,924 shares outstanding, before equitization lifted common shares to 88.6 million, so current stakes are lower.
findings.issue: "so current stakes are lower" assumes each holder's share count is unchanged since August 29, 2025 (Vanguard's since February 2024), and the surface does not show that. What the surface supports is narrower: the same holdings would be a smaller percentage of today's larger share count.
findings.fix: Write "so the same holdings would now be a smaller percentage" instead of asserting that current stakes are lower.
